FastAPI — codebase report

Built 2026-11-13 at commit 5758a9c83

FastAPI is a Python web framework for building HTTP and WebSocket APIs from type-annotated functions. The package in fastapi/ builds on Starlette (ASGI routing and middleware) and Pydantic (validation and serialization), and it generates an OpenAPI schema and the Swagger UI and ReDoc pages from your route declarations. The repo also holds a large docs tree in many languages, a test suite bigger than the package, and scripts that build and translate the docs. A newcomer starts with fastapi/applications.py (the FastAPI class), then fastapi/routing.py (APIRouter, APIRoute and the request handler) and fastapi/dependencies/utils.py (dependency resolution). This report has 13 diagrams. It has no data model, sitemap, state, journey or swimlane chart, because the code has no database schema, page tree, status field or multi-role process to draw. History, hot files, module imports and co-change charts are rolled up, as each section says.

The stack

The chart shows the main parts of the fastapi package, the libraries it builds on, and the repo tooling. A path operation function that you write is registered on an APIRouter, which makes one APIRoute per path. Each APIRoute builds a request handler that calls solve_dependencies and uses ModelField (a wrapper around a Pydantic TypeAdapter) to validate and serialize. Start with these boxes, then read the sequence and flowchart diagrams for the detail.

Registering a path operation

The chart traces what happens when you write @app.get on a function. FastAPI.get hands the call to APIRouter, which merges prefix, tags and dependencies and then builds an APIRoute. APIRoute builds the dependant (the object that describes the function's parameters), the response field and the request handler. The router then appends the route and bumps a version counter, so app.openapi() sees the new route.

Handling one HTTP request

The chart traces one HTTP request from the ASGI server to the response. On the first call FastAPI builds its middleware stack, and the request passes through it to the router, which finds the matching APIRoute. The request handler reads the body, calls solve_dependencies, and then either runs your function and serializes the result or raises RequestValidationError. This path is the core of the framework; read it before the dependency and body flowcharts.

A protected route rejects a request

The chart shows a request without an Authorization header reaching a route that depends on OAuth2PasswordBearer. solve_dependencies awaits the security object, and the object raises an HTTPException with status 401 and a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header. ExceptionMiddleware turns that exception into a JSON response. If the header is a valid bearer token, the token is passed to your function instead.

Building the OpenAPI schema and docs pages

The chart shows how FastAPI serves /docs and /openapi.json. The /docs page is plain HTML that loads the Swagger UI bundle from a CDN. The /openapi.json handler calls get_openapi, which collects the request and response models from all routes and builds one path item per route. The app caches the result and rebuilds it only when the router's routes version changes.

How solve_dependencies resolves one dependant

The flowchart shows the loop inside solve_dependencies. For each sub-dependant it solves the sub-dependant first (recursively), then reuses a cached value, enters a generator on an exit stack, awaits a coroutine, or runs a plain function in a thread pool. After the loop it validates path, query, header, cookie and body parameters, and injects Request, Response, BackgroundTasks and SecurityScopes. The function returns the values and any errors; the caller decides what to do with the errors.

How the request handler reads the body

The flowchart shows how the request handler decides what the request body is. A form body is read with request.form. Other bodies are read as bytes and parsed as JSON only when the Content-Type is application/json or a +json type, or when it is missing and strict content type is off. Invalid JSON becomes a RequestValidationError of type json_invalid; any other bytes stay raw.
